newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:
* A growing trend is inflating the severance packages for executives who have failed.
* The leader of SBC Communications, Edward Whitacre, disdains federal regulators while carving out an empire.
* A management shake-up at Rupert Murdoch's British Sky Broadcasting Plc has jarred investors.
* First Union has agreed to buy Signet Banking Corp for $3.3 billion.
* Technology is transforming the cattle and dairy industries.
* The business prospects of newspapers have improved sharply, with newsprint costs down and advertising up.
* Intel has settled a class action suit brought in the wake of the disclosure last year that an error in a testing process led the company to overstate the speed of some of its microprocessor chips.
* Mickey Mouse, who has helped sell films, videos and television shows, is headed onto radio, a medium that for decades has not been popular with children.
* Several million cars to be sold this autumn will get a costly new pollution-control device that will make it harder to fill the tank at some gas stations and may pose safety risks.
* Digital Theater Systems is mounting a challenge to the primacy of Dolby Laboratories in the audio world.
